title: Memetic Template Half-Life

validity_window.expiry_policy: if audience recognition collapses, demote to historical citation only

source_refs.author: Limor Shifman and digital folklore scholarship
source_refs.title: Memes in Digital Culture; template reuse and participatory mutation

observed_structure: a recognizable template circulates with stable relational slots
one role, caption function, or ownership condition mutates
meaning decays or inverts as recognition becomes ironic or exhausted
dramatic_operations: compress social conflict into a reusable frame
mark a culture's half-life through overuse
cinematic_affordances: repost chain as montage of ownership loss
cultural_scope: time-sensitive internet artifact; provenance and current usage context must be checked
misuse_risks: assuming global recognition of a local meme
transferable_structure: a circulating template acquires new charge when one relational role changes while enough structure remains recognizable
non_transferable_surface: direct duplication of copyrighted meme images or platform-specific branding
provenance_notes: Explicit time-sensitive cultural-signal pack; pair with audience recognition check.
